red_tests.failure_fingerprint: test_new_branch_push_validates_only_the_pushed_commit: the gate checked a commit set that is not exactly the pushed head, because the range is computed from unpublished local history; test_new_branch_push_still_blocks_on_the_pushed_commit: the pushed commit was not checked at all

correction_reason: new-branch pushes validate the entire unpublished local history, so the gate reports failures for commits that are not part of the push
rationale: Bind the new-branch range computation to KAN-218: the hook uses `git rev-list <sha> --not --remotes`, which cannot subtract anything for a branch with no remote-tracking ref, so the range becomes the whole unpublished history. Pin both halves of the fix: the range must contain exactly the pushed commit, and narrowing it must not stop the gate from validating and rejecting that commit.
